clue.text: Emaciation in a scalp

parts.note: a scalp taken from a defeated enemy was kept as a trophy

explanation.surface: Someone appears gaunt and wasted in the face and head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scalp' looks like part of the body but is the noun for a trophy of victory; 'in' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Wasting away of the body or a part of it is the medical sense of the word, the same as extreme thinness.

clue.text: Made trams specially — for this city, perhaps

indicators.note: specially suggests arranged in a particular way, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Trams have been built to order for a particular city.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dutch capital, famous for canals and its tram network, is a city.

clue.text: There are no returns from its other bank

definitions.text: There are no returns from its other bank

parts.words: There are no returns from its other bank
parts.note: reads like a banking complaint, but describes a river whose crossing by Caesar meant there was no turning back

explanation.definitionFit: Julius Caesar crossed this stream in 49 BC, an irrevocable step, so crossing it means passing a point of no return.

clue.text: Bit by bit, church is dividing things to eat

indicators.note: dividing means the abbreviation for church splits the food words apart

parts.note: a pie and a meal are things to eat
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A church shares out food portions gradually.
explanation.walkthrough: 'things to eat' supplies two foods, not one, and 'dividing' tells the church abbreviation to sit between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something gradually, a piece at a time, is the adverb's meaning.

clue.text: It's tolerable in the old form of oppression

indicators.note: in means the word for tolerable is placed inside the old word for the

parts.note: ye is an archaic spelling of the
OK means acceptable or tolerable

explanation.surface: A mild version of old-fashioned tyranny is said to be bearable.
explanation.definitionFit: A wooden harness across oxen's necks became a figure for servitude and subjugation.

clue.text: Sent back increased bill to rent house in Verona

indicators.note: something sent back is returned, so the word for bill is written in the opposite direction

parts.note: prices that are up have increased
AC, short for account, is a bill
to let a property is to rent it out

explanation.surface: Someone returns an inflated invoice for renting a home in the Italian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sent back' turns the whole of 'increased bill', UP plus AC, into CAPU. The house is a family, as in Shakespeare's Romeo and Juliet.
explanation.definitionFit: Juliet's family in Shakespeare's Verona tragedy, the rivals of the Montagues, is a noble house.

clue.text: 20% of nickel I put in category C

parts.note: a nickel is the US five-cent coin, so one fifth of it is a cent
a grade is a category or class

explanation.surface: Someone files a fifth of a coin under the letter C.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put in' just links the pieces; C stands for the temperature scale.
explanation.definitionFit: The Celsius temperature scale is abbreviated to its initial after a reading in degrees.

clue.text: Soldier captured on king's authority

parts.note: a POW is a prisoner of war
ER can stand for Edwardus Rex, King Edward

explanation.surface: A captured soldier claims to act by the king's command.
explanation.definitionFit: Control and the right to command someone is a kind of might.

clue.text: Take off clobber quietly, finishing with nothing on

parts.note: to lam someone is to beat or clobber them
p is piano, the musical direction for quietly
the figure 0 for nothing looks like O
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone strips off their clothes quietly until they are wearing nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clobber' looks like British slang for clothes, but here it is a verb meaning beat.
explanation.definitionFit: To take off someone is to mock them by imitation, which is a satire or send-up.

clue.text: A large cask is provided for the port

parts.note: a tun is a large beer or wine barrel

explanation.surface: A big barrel is supplied for some fortified wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' looks like the wine that fills a cask; it is a harbour city.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital of Tunisia is a Mediterranean harbour city.

clue.text: Buyer's first into bargain even to get fur

indicators.note: into means the letter is placed inside the word for bargain

parts.note: a sale offers goods at a bargain

indicators.note: the first of the word Buyer's is its opening letter only

explanation.surface: A shopper goes first into a bargain event and comes away with a fur coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' puts B inside SALE; 'even to get' only links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The dark pelt of a small Siberian marten is prized as a luxurious coat material.

clue.text: Frantic winks warning some relatives

indicators.note: something frantic is wild and disordered, so the letters of winks are jumbled

parts.note: an omen is a warning sign

explanation.surface: Someone winks wildly as a signal to certain family members.
explanation.definitionFit: Female members of one's family, such as aunts and nieces, are relatives.

clue.text: Artist and others joining that woman

parts.note: etc. abbreviates et cetera, meaning and others
her refers to that woman

explanation.surface: A painter and others meet up with a particular woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A printmaker who cuts designs into metal plates with acid is a kind of artist.

clue.text: Terrible reports I produced for class of buffoons

indicators.note: terrible suggests something badly mangled, so the letters of reports I are rearranged

explanation.surface: A child's dreadful school reports reveal a classroom full of clowns.
explanation.definitionFit: Clowns in white faces and loose costumes from French pantomime form a recognised type of buffoon.

clue.text: Preserve the outcome of this spell of improvisation?

definitions.text: Preserve the outcome of this spell of improvisation?

parts.note: jam is a fruit preserve
a session is a spell of activity

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a burst of improvised music should be recorded for posterity.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal gathering of musicians playing unrehearsed is a period of improvised music.

clue.text: Agreed to listen to poet

indicators.note: to listen to means the word is judged by how it sounds when spoken

parts.note: a deal that is done has been agreed

explanation.surface: Someone consents to hear a poetry reading.
explanation.walkthrough: John Donne was the English metaphysical poet.
explanation.definitionFit: John Donne was a seventeenth-century English writer of metaphysical verse.

clue.text: Frank and I are reforming this white man

indicators.note: reforming means shaping anew, so the letters of the words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Frank and I are trying to change a man's attitudes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reforming' rearranges FRANK plus I ARE; 'and' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An Afrikaans-speaking South African of Dutch descent was a white man in the apartheid-era sense.

clue.text: Jerk violently with sudden movement to get engine going

parts.note: to kick is to jerk the leg out violently
a start is a sudden involuntary movement

explanation.surface: A rider jerks hard on a pedal to fire up a motorcycle engine.
explanation.definitionFit: Starting a motorbike by stamping a pedal down sets the motor running.

clue.text: Blues used in service

parts.note: royal blue is a shade of blue
navy blue is another shade of blue

explanation.surface: Blue uniforms are worn in the armed forces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used in' only links the two colours to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Britain's sea-going armed force is one of the services.

clue.text: Rabble I conducted outside is ready to fight

parts.note: a rabble is a mob

indicators.note: outside means the word for conducted goes around the word is

parts.note: to conduct is to lead, so conducted gives led

explanation.surface: A mob says it led others out and now stands prepared for battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ready to fight' is the past participle used as an adjective; 'outside' wraps the verb for conducted round the clue's own 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Troops called up and assembled for active service are prepared for war.

clue.text: Book about Commonwealth soldier's endless source of wealth

parts.note: on means about, concerning

indicators.note: endless means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: an Anzac is a soldier from Australia or New Zealand

explanation.surface: A book about an Australian soldier tells of unlimited riches.
explanation.definitionFit: A rich vein of ore, and so any windfall, is a source of riches.

clue.text: Guarded and put in prison at journey's end

parts.note: to cage someone is to lock them up

indicators.note: the end of the word journey's is its final letter

explanation.surface: A traveller is locked up when the trip is over and becomes wary.
explanation.definitionFit: Being secretive and cautious about giving information is a guarded manner.

clue.text: Rock formed in great upheaval

indicators.note: an upheaval is a violent disturbance, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A rock was created in a great geological upheaval.
explanation.definitionFit: A hard igneous stone made of quartz and feldspar is a type of rock.

clue.text: Exhibit chap provided is in Paris

parts.note: a chap is a man
provided that means if
est is French for is

explanation.surface: A man has an exhibition in Paris, provided he gets one.
explanation.definitionFit: To show or display something clearly is to make it plain, a verb sense.

clue.text: Mineral in 21 hard to find in this book

parts.note: mica is one of the minerals in granite, the answer to 21 Down
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A mineral in rock is hard to find in a geology book.
explanation.definitionFit: A prophet's book in the Old Testament is a book of the Bible.

clue.text: It's one side of stone, in truth

definitions.text: It's one side of stone, in truth

indicators.note: in means the letter for one side goes inside the word for truth

parts.note: a fact is a truth
E, east, is one side or point of the compass

explanation.surface: A gem cutter states the plain truth about one face of a jewel.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines; 'in' puts E inside FACT.
explanation.definitionFit: A cut gem has many flat polished planes, each one a face of the jewel.

clue.text: Republic is having unfortunate king sent back

indicators.note: sent back means the king's name is written backwards

parts.note: King Lear is Shakespeare's tragic, ill-fated king

explanation.surface: A republic deposes and exiles its hapless monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A Middle Eastern parliamentary state founded in 1948 is a republic.

clue.text: Bash using upraised clubs or knife

indicators.note: upraised means lifted up, so in a down entry the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: bats are clubs used in games

explanation.surface: Someone attacks with a raised club or a blade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bash' also means a try at something, another sense of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To pierce someone with a blade is a verb sense of the word.

clue.text: One didn't volunteer to prepare to play one's part

parts.note: to con is an old word meaning to study or learn by heart
an actor's script holds the lines of their part

explanation.surface: An actor who never wanted the role must still learn his lines.
explanation.walkthrough: To con a script is to learn it before going on stage; 'to play' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: A recruit compelled by law into military service did not enlist by choice.

clue.text: Inner personality shown by Manx cat, for example?

indicators.note: a Manx cat has no tail, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a cat is an example of an animal

explanation.surface: A tailless cat seems to show its true inner self.
explanation.walkthrough: Manx cats, from the Isle of Man, are born without tails.
explanation.definitionFit: In Jungian psychology the soul or inner self, especially its feminine side, goes by this Latin term.

clue.text: Encourage to try PM's number

parts.note: a judge tries or hears a case
the British Prime Minister lives at number 10 Downing Street

explanation.surface: Someone urges the Prime Minister's team on.
explanation.walkthrough: 10 Downing Street is the official London residence of the UK Prime Minister.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone courage or cheer is to embolden them.

clue.text: Grossly flattering in storeroom

definitions.meaning: buttering someone up is flattering them crudely
a room in a college for storing provisions and drink

explanation.definitionFit: Laying it on thick like butter describes gushing praise; separately, a pantry for food and liquor in a college is so named.
